note: Hand-picked recent AI reporting from large, reputable newsrooms, links verified. Source mix is limited by access tooling: WSJ, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg are blocked from automated browsing, so the openable/verified set skews CNBC, AP (wire) and MIT Technology Review. The updater (8×/day) can broaden sources over time.

items.title: SK Hynix, SoftBank shares plunge as tech stocks in Asia track Wall Street chip sell-off
items.blurb: SK Hynix fell more than 8% and Samsung 7.9% as a US semiconductor sell-off spread to Asian markets.

items.title: How Red Bull's F1 team is using AI to make split-second decisions for Max Verstappen
items.blurb: Red Bull and Oracle built an AI strategy agent that helps engineers interpret Formula 1 rules and past rulings on race day.

items.title: IMF warns global economy nearing "limits of resilience"
items.blurb: The IMF says growing reliance on the AI investment boom leaves the world economy more exposed to shocks.

items.title: TikTok CEO sees major scientific breakthroughs from AI within three years
items.blurb: Shou Zi Chew expects AI-driven advances in physics, biotech and materials, and warns autonomous systems raise large cybersecurity risks.

items.title: IMF warns of AI 'tsunami' for job seekers
items.blurb: IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva says AI is hitting labor markets like a slow-moving tsunami, with young graduates affected first.

items.title: Intel, Broadcom CEOs warn capital crunch could become AI's biggest bottleneck
items.blurb: Broadcom's Hock Tan says financing may limit the AI buildout more than chips or power, with compute demand outrunning supply through 2029.

items.title: An AI pivot will drive Salesforce shares higher, says Bank of America
items.blurb: Bank of America moved Salesforce from underperform to buy, betting its shift toward AI products will lift the stock.

items.title: Microsoft to rely more on homegrown AI chips, reducing dependence on Nvidia
items.blurb: Microsoft unveiled its third-generation Maia accelerator and says its own chips will handle most incoming AI requests.

items.title: Did an AI or human write that paper? New detector decides by examining its ideas
items.blurb: A tool called IdeaLens judges whether a paper's ideas, not just its prose, came from a person or a machine.

items.title: Meta debuts Muse Wonder AI model in latest test of users' willingness to pay
items.blurb: Meta's most advanced model reaches developers now and paying Muse subscribers next, a test of AI revenue beyond ads.

items.title: Meta unveils new frontier-class AI models to compete with OpenAI, Anthropic
items.blurb: Muse Wonder and Wonder Full, code-named Watermelon, match or top rivals on agent, memory and coding tasks, Meta says.

items.title: Award-winning microscopy image disqualified over AI use
items.blurb: A winning entry in a major microscopy contest was pulled, prompting debate over AI in scientific imagery.

items.title: Global economy to slow less than expected in 2026 as AI boom offsets war hit: IMF
items.blurb: The IMF raised its 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1%, saying AI investment helped offset the energy shock from war.

items.title: AI is automating coding. So why are software developer job postings on the rise?
items.blurb: Developer postings are up almost 15% since early 2025, led by senior and AI roles, while entry-level hiring keeps weakening.

items.title: AI's quiet safety gatekeepers are stepping into the spotlight
items.blurb: Independent testers such as METR are drawing far more funding and attention as labs and governments lean on outside safety checks.

items.title: Hollywood takes on Zuckerberg, Musk and Altman amid widespread anxiety over AI
items.blurb: A run of films targets tech leaders as polls show most Americans worry about AI's risks and data centers.

items.title: Nvidia GPUs are everywhere. Here are the ways companies are accessing them
items.blurb: A guide to how companies buy, rent and finance Nvidia chips as demand for AI computing keeps growing.

items.title: Stocks saw new highs and big declines: How the volatile AI trade moved last week's market
items.blurb: AI stocks fell on an OpenAI revenue shortfall, then recovered; the S&P 500 still gained 1.2% for the week.

items.title: AI is changing how lawyers work — and putting the billable hour under pressure
items.blurb: Nearly 90% of UK and Irish legal professionals now use AI, and firms report handling more work without adding staff.

items.title: Microsoft's Nadella says AI needs an 'emergency brake' that humans control
items.blurb: Nadella called for containment, independent controls and a way for authorized people to pause or shut down a model mid-task.

items.title: Nvidia-backed Aussie AI firm Firmus withdraws historic IPO, citing market volatility
items.blurb: The data-center operator had sought about $5 billion; the pullback follows a sell-off in AI stocks.

items.title: CNBC Daily Open: What happened to the $20 billion?
items.blurb: OpenAI's annualized revenue came in at $50 billion, well under earlier reports, unsettling investors in AI stocks.

items.title: OpenAI denies researchers were fired for speaking out about AI concerns
items.blurb: OpenAI says three dismissed safety researchers committed a significant breach of trust and were not fired for raising concerns.

items.title: Scoop: AI companies plot "day after" scenarios for public revolt
items.blurb: Executives at Anthropic, OpenAI and others are privately planning for the political backlash after a catastrophic AI event, most likely a cyberattack.
